maya: FYI opening thread for CS-1492 (BrightMetric) 
They started getting 401s and `invalid signature` errors after we rolled their SSO IdP keys this AM. Support dump attached below.

ops-bot: jwks-rotation-deploy complete by @devops at 2026-04-02T08:15Z :white_check_mark:

support-agent: customer note: users can still login to IdP, but our API calls that validate tokens are failing with `Signature verification failed` or `unsupported algorithm: PS256` in some regions.

samir: can you paste the raw token header they sent and the jwks URL? do we have edge logs showing 3xx or 301 from jwks requests? :eyes:

support-agent: paste (redacted):
``
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJQUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6InByb3RvX2EyIn0....
JWKS URL: https://sso.brightmetric.example/.well-known/jwks.json
``
They said their IdP recently switched signing algorithm from RS256 to PS256 and also introduced an intermediate redirect for the jwks URL which their CDN cached as a 301.

jen: repro notes I ran locally:
1) simulate IdP rotating to PS256 and returning a JWKS with `kid: proto_a2` and `alg: PS256`.
2) our CDN (global-edge) cached an HTTP 301 for the jwks URL pointing to `https://auth.cdn.brightmetric.example/jwks` with a long TTL (1d). The edge cached the redirect and rewrote requests to the old backend which still served an RS256-only keyset.

curl steps (local repro):
``
# simulate edge cached redirect returning stale jwks from old backend
echo "HTTP/1.1 301 Moved Permanently\nLocation: https://auth.cdn.brightmetric.example/jwks\nCache-Control: max-age=86400" > redirect.cached
# request jwks via edge (follows cached redirect):
curl -i -L --header "Accept: application/json" https://sso.brightmetric.example/.well-known/jwks.json
# output contains only RS256 keyset (no PS256 kid)
# verification fails: unsupported alg or kid not found
```

samir: interesting — two separate problems combined: (1) algorithm change from RSASSA-PSS to RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 and (2) CDN cached a redirect which landed us at a backend still on old keyset. verifier logs show both `kid mismatch` and `unsupported alg: PS256` depending on region.

kyle: immediate customer mitigation we applied: purged the redirect entry on the CDN for BrightMetric's jwks path and added a temporary header override `cache-control: max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=30` for `.well-known/jwks.json` for that tenant. Also advised BrightMetric to re-issue tokens signed with RS256 for a short overlap window. That restored API validation in ~12 minutes for most regions.

jen: additional edge case I found: some clients had tokens where header `alg` was `PS256` but the JWKS entry for the new key included `alg` omitted (per RFC this is allowed). Our verifier currently requires `alg` in the JWKS to match the token `alg`. That caused `unsupported algorithm` even though the key itself would verify.

maya: support note 
customer also reported a ~6m clock skew on some app servers which triggered `exp` failures during retries. so multiple causes: redirect cache, alg mismatch handling, and clock skew.

samir: short-term fixes we pushed to verifier config:
- relax strict `alg` comparison: if JWKS key lacks `alg` but the key type (kty) and curve/params match token alg, allow verification. (with a logged audit event)
- on `kid` not found or `alg` mismatch, trigger an async one-shot JWKS refresh and retry verification once.
- treat 3xx caching headers specially for `.well-known` endpoints: do not cache redirects longer than 60s, and preserve query on cache key.

jen: proposed code change (PR 5382) includes singleflight dedupe for background JWKS fetches and adds an explicit check for ECDSA vs RSA vs PS signing families. Also added a fallback that will try verifying across all compatible keys when `kid` absent (with rate-limited extra CPU).

kyle: infra/security asks before we bake the fallback:
- require tenant opt-in for algorithm relaxation (some customers want alg pinning for security)
- rate-limit cross-key verification attempts per tenant (avoid CPU amplification)
- add telemetry: `auth.verifier.alg_mismatch.count`, `auth.jwks.redirect_cached.count`, and `auth.jwks.refresh_latency_ms`

security-alert-bot: jwks-rotation-detected: brightmetric-2026-04-02 
rotation-owner: @brightmetric-idp-admin :warning:

maya: customer-facing resolution summary for CS-1492: we purged CDN redirect, applied short-term cache override for jwks, applied verifier retry logic, and recommended BrightMetric include a 10m overlap period where tokens signed with previous alg are accepted. Customer confirmed recovery at ~08:27Z and asked for a short postmortem.

samir: long-term actions (owners):
- (samir) merge PR 5382: async refresh + singleflight + retry on kid/alg mismatch 
due: EOD
- (kyle) CDN patch: do not cache 301/302 from identity providers for more than 60s; add runbook for emergency redirect purge 
due: tomorrow
- (jen) add integration tests for: redirect-cached-jwks, alg-absent-jwks, and client clock-skew scenarios 
due: next week
- (maya) draft customer postmortem and notify support policy owners to add guidance for IdP alg rotations 
due: 48h

jen: reproduction artifacts pushed to internal gist: https://gist.internal/brightmetric-rot-repro 
do not share externally.

maya: root cause summary for postmortem: identity provider changed signing algorithm and introduced a redirect; CDN cached that redirect and routed to an old backend missing the new keyset, our verifier was strict on `alg` metadata and did not attempt a JWKS refresh on `kid`/`alg` mismatch, and some customer infra had clock skew amplifying failures. Combined produced widespread validation errors.

kyle: +1 on telemetry dashboard. added to infra backlog: `auth.jwks.redirect_cached.count` alert if >5 in 5m for any tenant.

maya: thanks. if you see more CS tickets mentioning `unsupported algorithm` or `redirect cached` tag me and I'll triage. :thumbsup:
